text:
Molecular formula: C₉H₁₁NO₂  

Index of hydrogen deficiency (IHD) = C – H/2 + N/2 + 1  
= 9 – 11/2 + 1/2 + 1 = 5 → an aromatic ring (4) + one extra π-bond/ ring (carbonyl).

IR data  
• 3420 and 3325 cm⁻¹: two N–H stretches → primary amine (–NH₂).  
• 1720 cm⁻¹: ester C=O (amide C=O would appear lower, ~1650–1680 cm⁻¹).  
So the molecule must contain both –NH₂ and an ester group.

¹H-NMR data  
1. 1.20 ppm, triplet, 3 H  
2. 4.50 ppm, quartet, 2 H  
 ⇒ an ethyl group bound through oxygen: –O–CH₂(4.5)–CH₃(1.2).  
3. 4.0 ppm, broad singlet, 2 H → NH₂ protons.  
4. 7.0 ppm (d, 2 H) and 8.0 ppm (d, 2 H) → para-disubstituted benzene (AA′BB′ pattern).

Comparison with choices  

A) 4-Aminophenyl propionate  
   – phenyl-O–CO–CH₂CH₃.  The ethyl group is on the acyl side (CH₂ next to C=O would appear ~2.3 ppm, not 4.5 ppm). No O–CH₂ signal at 4.5 ppm → does NOT match NMR.

B) Ethyl 4-aminobenzoate  
   –O–CH₂CH₃ ethyl ester attached to the benzoate carbonyl; NH₂ para to CO₂Et.  
   Gives O–CH₂ quartet (~4.5 ppm), CH₃ triplet (~1.2 ppm), NH₂ broad ~4 ppm, and para-aromatic 7.0/8.0 ppm doublets. Fits IR and formula perfectly.

C) N-(4-Ethoxyphenyl)formamide  
   Contains an amide (C=O ~1660 cm⁻¹) and only one N–H stretch; would show a formyl (CHO) proton ~8–9 ppm. IR/NMR don’t match.

D) 3-Ethoxybenzamide  
   Amide carbonyl (≈1660 cm⁻¹) and only one N–H stretch; aromatic pattern would not be two equal doublets (meta-substitution). IR/NMR don’t match.

Thus the only structure consistent with all data is ethyl 4-aminobenzoate.

Answer: B
